blocks.text:
Leave early in the morning for the Argentine side. Iguazú National Park has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1984.

An ecological train runs through the park. The three main walking trails start near its stops.

**Lower Circuit:** about 1,700 metres, approximately 1 hour 45 minutes, moderate difficulty. The paths lead to viewpoints below the falls. This circuit takes in the Alvar Núñez, Elenita, Lanusse and Bossetti falls. At Bossetti, the water drops in an almost unbroken curtain.

**Upper Circuit:** about 1,300 metres, approximately 1 hour, easy. The paths give you a view of the upper river before it spills over the edge. Notable falls along the circuit include Adam and Eve.

**Devil’s Throat:** about 1,000 metres, approximately 1.5 hours, moderate difficulty. This is the high point of the route. The water drops about 82 metres. Thick spray hangs over the gorge, and you can hear the roar well before you reach the main viewing platform.

After the tour, transfer back to the hotel.

On the Argentine side, you get much closer to the water. The cascades rise above you on the Lower Circuit. The Upper Circuit follows the river’s edge, and the boardwalk to Devil’s Throat crosses the broad riverbed. The contrast with the previous day is clear. The Brazilian bank gives you the sweeping panorama, while the Argentine trails bring you much closer to the individual falls.

blocks.text:
After breakfast, transfer to Iguazú airport and fly to Rio. On arrival, you will be met and driven to Angra dos Reis on the Green Coast. Check in at the hotel.

Angra dos Reis is surrounded by islands and sheltered bays. The archipelago has 365 islands, one for each day of the year. Ilha Grande is the largest. It remained closed for a long time, which helped preserve its natural areas. Today it is known above all for its protected landscapes and beaches.

The name Angra dos Reis is associated with “Bay of Kings”. The water in the sheltered bays is calmer than along the open Atlantic coast. Here you can go diving, surfing or fishing, or sail between the islands on a yacht.

The pace changes after the first week. Early departures and busy sightseeing days give way to quiet bays, boats tied up at the piers and time to choose how you spend the day. The water ranges from deep green offshore to almost clear by the shore. The mild climate and abundance of islands make boat trips a natural choice here.
